newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Major Slovak shares mixed, SAX firms 0.88 points.
newsitem.headline: Major Slovak shares mixed, SAX firms 0.88 points.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to Nafta pushing the SAX index up 0.88 points to 204.70.
Brokers said interest in equities trading seemed to be slowing down after a significant increase in activity last week.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta gained 45 crowns to close at 1,970, but brokers said the very small volume of Nafta shares traded made it difficult to predict future developments.
Oil refiner Slovnaft led Monday's trading on the BSE floor, with 56,010 shares traded, closing down 25 crowns to 910.
But brokers said the two largest blocks, totalling 50,000 shares, were sold for 935 crowns.

"There is quite a large amount of Slovnaft shares available on the market at the moment, and the price of around 935 crowns appears to be well accepted both by sellers and buyers," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Sykora said there seemed to be foreign interest in Slovnaft, and that the price was not expected to decline in the short-term.
Steel producer VSZ closed unchanged at 650 crowns, with brokers predicting an upturn soon on the grounds that larger packages were only available for around 670 crowns.

Slovakia's largest commercial bank, VUB, closed unchanged at 1,750 crowns, but the share was traded at around 1,680 for most of the day. Dealers said the closing price was pulled up artificially on speculative buying.
Overall, volume fell to 381,572 shares, from 429,300 on Friday, while turnover rose to 330.74 million crowns, from 239.19 million.
